text: Mr A. Navalnyy launched a nationwide campaign called "He is not our Tsar".
The campaign "He is not our Tsar" consisted of holding rallies on 5 May 2018 to protest against the forthcoming inauguration of Mr V. Putin as the President of the Russian Federation.
The election of Mr V. Putin as President of the Russian Federation took place on 18 March 2018.
Ms P. notified the Cheboksary town administration of her intention to hold a public event in the form of a march and a meeting.
The Cheboksary town administration informed Ms P. that the itinerary for the march included areas where public events were not allowed under the regional legislation.
The Cheboksary town administration invited Ms P. to hold a meeting instead of the planned march and meeting event.
The Cheboksary town administration invited Ms P. to hold the meeting in one of the specially designated areas approved by the regional government in its Decree no. 598 of 26 December 2012.
The specially designated area proposed by the Cheboksary town administration was specifically at Sosnovskaya Street, next to a church, a local police station and a children's park.
Ms P. replied to the Cheboksary town administration indicating her disagreement with the proposed alternative venue.
According to the applicants, the venue mentioned by the Cheboksary town administration remained within the town borders of Cheboksary.
According to the applicants, the distance between the venue proposed by the Cheboksary town administration and the initially proposed venue amounted to some fifty kilometres.

According to the applicants, the venue proposed by the Cheboksary town administration had poor transport and public infrastructure which would have been impracticable for the presence of hundreds of participants.
The Cheboksary town administration's decision regarding Ms P.'s notice was subsequently upheld on judicial review.

On 5 May 2018 people assembled into a non-approved rally in Cheboksary.
The non-approved rally on 5 May 2018 was held in a different manner as compared to the notice lodged by Ms P.
At 2 p.m. on 5 May 2018 at Respublika Square in Cheboksary, according to the applicants, the police ordered the demonstrators to cease the meeting.
According to the applicants, the police threatened the demonstrators at Respublika Square with use of force when ordering them to cease the meeting.
After the police order at Respublika Square, the demonstrators started to move through the main town streets of Cheboksary, walking on the pavements to avoid disruption of traffic.
The demonstrators moving through the main town streets of Cheboksary were followed by the police.
At Chapayev Square in Cheboksary, the demonstrators were met by another police squad and dispersed.
According to the authorities, the applicants did not comply with the police order to cease participation in the meeting at Respublika Square on 5 May 2018.
According to the authorities, from 2.30 to 4 p.m. on 5 May 2018, the applicants participated in an event at Chapayev Square in Cheboksary.
The authorities and the courts classified the event at Chapayev Square on 5 May 2018 as a "demonstration" under the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act).
According to the authorities, the applicants did not comply with the police order to cease participation in the demonstration at Chapayev Square on 5 May 2018.
At Respublika Square, the police made several warnings informing the demonstrators of the unlawful nature of their presence in a public place and required them to cease their unlawful activities.
At Chapayev Square, the police made several warnings informing the demonstrators of the unlawful nature of their presence in a public place and required them to cease their unlawful activities.
On 15 May 2018 the Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary examined two separate cases concerning Mr Raymov's participation in the meeting and the demonstration on 5 May 2018.
The Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary examined the two separate cases concerning Mr Raymov at two hearings on 15 May 2018.

In the case concerning Mr Raymov's participation in the meeting, the Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary convicted him under Article 20.2 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences and sentenced him to a fine of 10,000 Russian roubles (approximately 135 euros at the time).

In the case concerning Mr Raymov's participation in the demonstration, the Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary convicted him under Article 20.2 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences and sentenced him to a fine of 20,000 Russian roubles (approximately 270 euros at the time).
Mr Raymov appealed against the convictions, arguing that he had exercised his freedom of peaceful assembly by taking part in one single event.
Mr Raymov argued on appeal that it had been unjustified to prosecute and punish him separately for two parts of the same event.
On 5 June 2018 the Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic held appeal hearings in each of the two cases concerning Mr Raymov.
The Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic upheld the trial judgments in both cases concerning Mr Raymov.

The Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic stated that Mr Raymov had violated section 6 § 3 of the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act) because he had not complied with the orders to disperse given during the meeting and demonstration.
The Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic stated that Mr Raymov had been prosecuted for different facts in the two separate cases.

In a separate third set of proceedings, Mr Raymov was convicted under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences in relation to his non-compliance with the order to disperse during the meeting on 5 May 2018.
The appeal court set aside the judgment convicting Mr Raymov under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences and discontinued the proceedings for lack of corpus delicti.

The appeal court discontinued the proceedings against Mr Raymov under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences pursuant to a recent resolution by the Plenary Supreme Court of the Russian Federation on the application of the lex specialis rule in cases concerning rallies.

The resolution by the Plenary Supreme Court of the Russian Federation on the application of the lex specialis rule in cases concerning rallies is referenced in Korneyeva v. Russia, no. 72051/17, §§ 25 and 60, 8 October 2019.

On 9 June 2018 the Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary examined charges against Mr Ryabenko under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences on account of his participation in the meeting on 5 May 2018.

On 9 June 2018 the Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary examined charges against Mr Ryabenko under Article 20.2 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences on account of his participation in the meeting on 5 May 2018.
Mr Ryabenko was sentenced to a fine of 10,500 Russian roubles in the proceedings concerning his participation in the meeting on 5 May 2018.
The Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary took note of the existence of a final decision by which the Cheboksary town administration's reply to Ms P.'s notice had been upheld on judicial review.
The Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary found that Mr Ryabenko had taken part in a non-notified public event consisting of a meeting, which had then transformed into a demonstration.
The Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary found that Mr Ryabenko had not complied with the repeated orders from the police requiring the termination of the event on 5 May 2018.

The Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary stated that the event's organisers had defined its topic as protection of citizens' rights, while the slogans and speeches during the event were in breach of that topic.

The Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary stated that the slogans and speeches during the event on 5 May 2018 amounted in substance to a negative assessment of the person who had been elected to the post of the President of the Russian Federation.

The Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary stated that the slogans and speeches during the event on 5 May 2018 did not contain an indication of any civic views or deficiencies in the functioning of the State or proposals for improvements.

In separate proceedings, on 9 June 2018 the Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary convicted Mr Ryabenko under Article 20.2 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences on account of his participation in the demonstration on 5 May 2018.
Mr Ryabenko was sentenced to up to twenty hours of community work in the proceedings concerning his participation in the demonstration on 5 May 2018.

On 10 July 2018 the Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic, reviewing the judgment of the Leninskiy District Court of Cheboksary described in paragraph 8 of the judgment, set aside the conviction of Mr Ryabenko under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

On 10 July 2018 the Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic upheld Mr Ryabenko's conviction for the offence under Article 20.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences relating to the meeting and reduced the fine to 10,000 Russian roubles.
On 10 July 2018 the same judge of the Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic also examined Mr Ryabenko's appeal against the judgment relating to the demonstration.

The Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic upheld Mr Ryabenko's conviction relating to the demonstration, considering that Mr Ryabenko had violated section 6 § 3 (1) of the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act).
The Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic found that Mr Ryabenko had committed a serious breach of public order and public safety in relation to the demonstration on 5 May 2018.

The Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic found that Mr Ryabenko's actions had entailed consequences consisting of the presence of numerous people on the pavements in the town centre of Cheboksary and near buildings hosting public authorities.

The Supreme Court of the Chuvashiya Republic found that Mr Ryabenko's actions had impeded the movement of pedestrians and had created a real threat of interfering with the authorities' functioning and other people's rights.
The Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act) defines a "public event" as an open, peaceful action accessible to all.

Under the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act), a public event may be held in the form of a gathering, a meeting, a demonstration, a march, or a picket, or in various combinations of these forms, as defined in section 2 of that Act.
Pursuant to sections 5 and 7 of the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act), the organiser of a public event must notify the executive or municipal authority of the event.
Under the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act), the procedure for notification of a public event is determined by a regional statute.
The notification procedure under the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act) is described in Navalnyy v. Russia [GC], nos. 29580/12 and 4 others, § 45, 15 November 2018.

Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at all locations mentioned in section 8 of the Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act).
Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at or near shopping malls or markets and within fifty metres of them.

Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at buildings hosting educational, children-related, cultural, medical or sports institutions and, until 2020, within fifty metres of those buildings.
Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at sports areas and children's playgrounds.
Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at religious buildings or objects and, until 2020, within fifty metres of them.
Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at buildings hosting municipal and public authorities and, until 2020, within thirty metres of them.
Under the Chuvashiya Republic's Statute no. 77 of 30 November 2012, public events were prohibited at entrances to residential buildings if the distance was less than five metres.
